Jordan_AE: Quick heads-up — FinTech POC asking for a dedicated pool with fixed outbound IPs so their payment partner can allowlist. They also need DNS resolution to resolve our endpoint to those IPs. Any infra/network blockers?
Emma_SE: We can do this two ways: 1) Reserve static egress IPs (EIPs) on the Dedicated pool, or 2) Private connectivity (VPC peering / PrivateLink / on-prem). For a quick POC static egress is fastest.
Lia (Customer NW): We're on Azure and their platform SNATs outbound by default. If you reserve EIPs on your side will that guarantee all outbound traffic originates from those IPs?
Sam_Infra: Short answer: yes for traffic that flows through the dedicated NAT path we provision, but caveats: we provision a NAT gateway/EIP pair per AZ to keep SNAT sticky. App-level retries across AZs can appear from different EIPs — let us know if partner requires a single IP.
Emma_SE: Also: our dedicated endpoints are fronted by a regional LB that terminates TLS. For DNS they should allowlist the reserved EIPs, not the hostname, since hostname can resolve to multiple IPs/regions. If they need DNS A records pinned we can provide the assigned IPs for the POC.
Lia (Customer NW): Partner requires inbound allowlist of our egress IPs and also to allow TCP 443 health checks from a /29. Can you confirm what ports/protocols to allow?
Sam_Infra: Ports to allow: 443 outbound (for API traffic). Health checks: HTTPS (443) from our health-check pool; we'll give you the CIDR. Also expect occasional DNS lookups (UDP 53) from our edge; if they block DNS at FW level, allow UDP 53 to our resolver IPs.
Emma_SE: Quick test people can run once we hand over IPs:
```
curl -v --resolve "api.redwood.example:443:203.0.113.7" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DEDI_KEY>" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
This forces host->IP mapping to verify connectivity without depending on public DNS.
Lia (Customer NW): Good. Timeline? We need to share the IPs with partner tomorrow.
Sam_Infra: If legal/network ok, we can reserve EIPs and update routing in ~48 hours. Public docs: https://redwood.example/docs/networking/static-egress (I'll attach the CIDRs in the ticket).
Emma_SE: Pricing note: static egress (reserved IPs + NAT) is a billable add-on for Dedicated POCs — one-time setup + monthly fee. I'll confirm exact number with finance and post here.
Sam_Infra: Created INF-5234 to track the EIP reservation + firewall CIDRs. Assigned: @Sam_Infra. ETA 48-72h. deploy-bot: INF-5234 created — link: https://redwood.example/tickets/INF-5234 :white_check_mark:
Jordan_AE: Awesome — I'll relay ETA/pricing to the customer and ask them to confirm partner accepts 3 IPs (we recommend 3 to avoid single-point AZ failover issues). :thumbsup:
Lia (Customer NW): Thanks, please add the health-check CIDR and any TLS SNI notes (they do SNI filtering on their LB).
Sam_Infra: Note on SNI: we send SNI for target hostnames, but for Dedicated POCs TLS termination happens at our regional front; partner should allow the IPs + SNI hostnames if they do host-based checks. If they need mTLS we can evaluate Private deployment.
Emma_SE: I'll follow up with pricing and drop the exact EIPs/CIDRs in INF-5234 once provisioned.
Jordan_AE: Perfect — moving to customer update now.
